newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Gov sees FY 1999 budget gap of $1.6 billion.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Gov sees FY 1999 budget gap of $1.6 billion.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki on Wednesday projected an up to $1.6 billion budget gap for fiscal 1999, but was confident that the potential problem could be handled.

New York State's lawmakers late Tuesday agreed a preliminary pact for fiscal 1998, which began on April 1. That $67 billion plan, which still must be approved, would deposit about $530 million of a projected $2.6 billion of extra revenues in a reserve fund.

Asked by Albany reporters about projected shortfalls in later years, Pataki said "(Fiscal) 1998-1999 is in the neighborhood of $1.5 or $1.6 billion, I believe is the projection, and we think that is totally manageable and that will be fine."

The Republican governor, whose 1998 fiscal budget plan was swiftly attacked by fiscal monitors as financially irresponsible, shrugged off the risk that an economic downturn might reduce state revenues.

"As I indicated, our projection for income receipts this year is very prudent. The actual increase in tax receipts in the 1996-1997 budget year was at least 10 percent. In 1997-1998, we are anticipating growth of half of that."
